persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.bridge: The father who cannot see you is what the Gita calls a mind clouded by its own picture. Your worth is not his to measure.
understanding.week_thesis: This week moves you from being unseen by the man you love to standing in the life you are building, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being seen as less than you are by the person you love, and the anger of it, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that his picture is his smallness, and that the only harm is letting it replace your own.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what you are cannot be cut smaller by what he sees.
week_beats.act: You try speaking the true thing to him, gently and firmly, and holding your ground on what is yours.

understanding.core_struggle: A student under twenty-five is being told by their father that films are for rich kids, pushed toward an MBA, and the fights leave the mother crying in the kitchen.
understanding.mirror: You love him, and still every night the kitchen fills with his words and her tears.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being seen as less than you are by the person you love most, and the anger of a home that fills with his words and her tears every night.
queries.diagnose: When a parent sees only a role, their picture is their smallness, not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what he sees; your worth was never his to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing, gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture he holds.
queries.story: A young seeker whose elders dismiss their path, who questioned them openly and stood in their truth until the room fell quiet.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the field. He tells him to take up his own path, even if it is flawed, rather than copying another person's duties perfectly. Doing the work that fits your own nature brings no guilt. It is an offering of your true self.
verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Prahasta
verse.setting: Prahasta, Ravana's son, leaves after his father rejects his advice and insults him.
verse.sanskrit: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
verse.line: Good advice won't take on someone set on ruin, like medicine on the dying.
verse.translation: How is it that sound advice doesn't take with you? Like medicine on one in death's grip. Seeing it was evening, Ravana went to his palace, admiring his twenty arms.
verse.why: Some people cannot hear good advice; give it, then stop beating yourself up.

prasang.title: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
prasang.summary: Mandodari, hearing the bridge is built, again begs Ravana to pick fights only where he can win, and to step back. Ravana boasts. His son Prahasta tells the court that flatterers are many and honest advisers few, and suggests first sending an envoy. Ravana insults him, and Prahasta leaves saying good advice cannot reach one set on ruin.
prasang.story_hook: The bridge was built, the army was across, and the king of Lanka was still laughing.
prasang.lesson: Some people cannot hear good advice; give it, then stop beating yourself up.

verse.meaning: Prahasta speaks to Ravana after his father rejects his wise counsel. He tells him that good advice cannot take root in someone determined to destroy themselves. Prahasta leaves, refusing to waste his breath on a mind that will not listen.
verse.for_you: Yesterday you saw your own path. Today you see his. His mind is set on ruin, and your good advice cannot reach him. Stop wasting your breath and let him hold his own smallness.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that the whole universe is strung on him, and he is pure awareness. Do not let your mind shrink into pettiness or worry. You are already vast and free.
verse.for_you: He calls your world a rich kid's game, but your awareness is wider than his words. Do not let his picture of you shrink the space you hold. You are not small.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom, and she tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and to stop fearing. The point is that past failure does not define a person, and those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: The father who cannot see you is what the Gita calls a mind clouded by its own picture. Your worth is not his to measure. You are building a life where films matter, and that vision is yours alone.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about the discipline of speech, saying it should cause no distress, be truthful, pleasant and beneficial. The point is that speech should be kind and true without cruelty, and it should be helpful.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today you try speaking the true thing to him, gently and firmly, and holding your ground on what is yours. You might say, I study films because this is who I am, and I need you to see that.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them. Ram says his words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained. They came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone. The point is that fear jumps ahead of facts, and calm, clear words build trust fast.
verse.for_you: When you speak to your father, let your words be clear and steady, not rushed or strained. You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.

story.title: Nachiketa questions his father's gift
story.story_hook: Nachiketa watched his father give away cows too old to give milk, and could not keep quiet.
story.summary: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.
story.lesson: A child's honest question can show up an adult's empty gesture.

weeks.title: Unseen by the one you love

script: You are angry because you feel invisible in your own home. Your father pushes an MBA and calls films for rich kids. The fights are loud. Your mother cries in the kitchen. You are carrying the weight of a house that will not see you.
Arjuna is in the middle of a war. He has laid down his bow. Krishna tells him to stop copying someone else's idea of a warrior. And Krishna replies:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna says do your own work, even if it is flawed. Copying another person's perfect path will still leave you empty. Your own path, walked honestly, brings no guilt. This is easier said than done, because your family wants a perfect copy of a life you do not want.
Tonight, close the door. Watch one film. Let the MBA talk be noise. You are not stealing time. You are tending the life you are actually building.
What if your worth is not his to measure?

depth.life: You sit with your phone, watching the same five hours of films your father calls a waste of time. The fights happen in the dark, and your mother cries in the kitchen. You are angry because you are being measured by a man who cannot see who you are becoming.
depth.points: Krishna tells Arjuna that doing your own work, with its flaws, is better than copying another's path perfectly. Your worth is not in the approval of the man who dismisses your nature.
depth.practice: Write down one small thing today that is truly yours, something no one else can do for you.
depth.question: What is one small thing today that is truly yours?
